opening.argument: The plan sets a $500 price per mining-pool share and ties that share to 1,000 days of mining and a stated 50% of profits. It also pays 20% on pool purchases by recruited team members, plus a 5% bonus tied to their first two personally enrolled people. These terms make recruitment, members’ purchases, and team activity part of the compensation structure, not simply participation in mining profits. The presentation describes commissions and layered team bonuses alongside the share-based profit claim. The available evidence does not establish whether mining or payments occurred, and it does not verify the linked destination; the case rests on what the plan asks viewers to buy and how it rewards recruitment.
